clusters.title: Injury and availability data engineering
clusters.decision: Do we archive the official report as a point-in-time series (so availability can be backtested), or keep reading it as a weekly page?
options: A. Daily automated capture of the official report
Creates the as-of history that every lab says is missing; storage is trivial; needs a scheduled job and a retention rule.
B. Manual weekly capture
No engineering, but the history is thin and the timestamps are not trustworthy - which is exactly the flaw already flagged in this repo.
C. Do nothing; treat injuries as commentary
Honest, and keeps the site free of un-backtested injury 'signals'.
clusters.why_now: The Friday report is not final, Monday's status is not published until Saturday, and an archived snapshot is the only way to know what was actually knowable pre-game.
clusters.owner_of_change: A session can build the capture; the owner chooses retention and licensing terms.

clusters.title: Validation gates and statistical rigour
clusters.decision: Which gate set is canonical, and are its thresholds (sample floor, correction, push handling, leakage tests) enforced in CI or only described?
options: A. Adopt the root ten-gate set as the single standard
One definition of 'passed'; every other hub reports against it; requires the labs' differing implementations to be labelled.
B. Keep per-lab gate sets, publish the differences
Preserves each lab's independence; leaves the same strategy passing in one lab and failing in another.
C. Strengthen the gates (bootstrap CIs, BH correction, minimum-events floor, push-inclusive settlement)
Fewer false positives; more candidates rejected, which is already the site's dominant outcome.
clusters.why_now: The audit found gate implementations that differ materially (push handling, repricing in G9, pooled ATS arithmetic); the leaderboard is only as trustworthy as that choice.
clusters.owner_of_change: A session can implement; the owner approves the standard.

rows.text: Hold a no-bet status quo until a strategy clears 10/10 gates
rows.detail: Formally keep allocation at zero and publish that decision on the landing page; re-open only when a strategy passes every gate in any lab.
rows.impact: Prevents capital from chasing noise; matches every lab's current 0-qualified result.

rows.text: Replace the pooled ATS 'coin-flip test' with a one-sided test
rows.detail: The headline '50.0%, p = 1.0' ATS result is an arithmetic identity: the sample contains every game twice, once per side, so exactly half the rows win. It cannot detect a market tilt in either direction, yet it is presented as evidence that the market is efficient.
rows.risk: The honest test is closer to significance, which invites over-reading. Publish the CI, not just the p-value.

rows.text: Add negative controls to every strategy batch and publish them next to the candidates
rows.detail: A screen that rejects everything looks rigorous, but it looks identical to a screen that is simply broken. Two controls already exist in the leaderboard; they are not shown as a diagnostic.
rows.risk: A clairvoyant control validates the plumbing only; it says nothing about whether a real edge exists.

rows.text: Write the settlement and void rules down before pricing anything
rows.detail: Parlay and prop settlement differ by operator (push handling, void legs, minimum leg count, same-game restrictions). A strategy that looks profitable under one rulebook can be unprofitable under another.
rows.risk: A single operator's rules will not generalise; the choice must be stated as a limitation.

rows.text: Put the price-sensitivity gate (G9) in front of every other gate
rows.detail: Every strategy currently fails G9 by construction because no executable price exists. The screen therefore rejects everything for one reason and the other nine gates do relatively little work.
rows.risk: Reordering the gates changes the published '5/10' style counts; those must be recomputed, not relabelled.

rows.text: State the sample-size floor for a 'signal' before testing, and publish it
rows.detail: The luck page computes 39,240 bets needed to detect a 51% win rate at 80% power, yet candidate strategies are presented with 137 to 649 bets. A reader has to do the arithmetic to see the screen cannot possibly distinguish skill.
rows.risk: Almost every candidate becomes 'not testable', which is the honest label but a less satisfying dashboard.

rows.text: Maintain 10-gate hard filter (NIST z-test, BH FDR q<0.10, Empirical Bayes > 0%) before capital allocation
rows.detail: Maintain 10-gate hard filter (NIST z-test, BH FDR q<0.10, Empirical Bayes > 0%) before capital allocation
rows.recommended: KEEP — Maintain strict 0% live bankroll deployment posture.
rows.impact: Protects bankroll from overfitting finite-sample noise and market vig.

clusters.title: Correlation, parlays and player-prop combos
clusters.decision: Do we price multi-leg bets with measured joint outcomes (and a published correlation matrix), or refuse to publish parlay edges at all?
options: A. Measure joint distributions from player box scores
Already partially done (QB-WR1 r = 0.562 in the root site) and reproducible; it prices correlation but not the operator's actual parlay price.
B. Wait for a parlay price archive, then price against the market
Correct comparison, blocked on T02.
C. No parlay content

method: Every suggestion published by a sibling hub is read from that hub's own JSON register, normalised to one row per hub proposal, then clustered by keyword rules (explicit overrides where a hub's wording was ambiguous). The cluster rank is arithmetic: 10 x number of hubs that proposed it, + 3 if any hub labelled it high priority, + 1 per other cluster it unblocks. No cluster contains a number that was typed in.
